players.name: Phil Salt
players.bio:
Powerful English batsman Phil Salt made his Big Bash debut in BBL|09 as an international signing with the Adelaide Strikers.

A heavy-hitting right-hander, Salt has played a key role with the Sussex Sharks in England's T20 Blast competition in recent seasons under coach Jason Gillespie and alongside fellow Strikers Rashid Khan and Alex Carey.

Renowned for his aggression at the top of the order and energy in the field, Salt made an immediate impact in his first Big Bash season with 361 runs at a strike rate of 164.09.

players.name: Jos Buttler
players.didyouKnow: In 2010, Butler was named the Young Wisden School's Cricketer of the Year.
players.bio:
Talented with the bat and behind the stumps, Jos Buttler is one of England’s most exciting talents.

Buttler came to the attention of selectors after impressive performances for Somerset and made his one-day international debut for England in 2012. His next chance in the ODI side came almost one year later and 2013 proved a bountiful year for the batsman, who scored two fifties and helped England finish runners-up in the Champions Trophy.

Buttler’s notched his first ODI hundred in May 2014, smashing 121 off 74 balls and his Test debut followed against India after Matt Prior stood down due to injury. He made an instant impact scoring 85 from 83 balls and excelled with the gloves to help England to a 266-run win.

Now playing with Lancashire in country cricket, Buttler’s main strengths with the bat are his aggression and inventiveness. After making his name in the Big Bash League, he is now a contracted player with the Rajasthan Royals in the IPL and widely regarded as one of England’s best short-form cricketers.

After an interrupted beginning to his Test career, Buttler now appears to have solidified his position as England’s first-choice keeper in all formats. He scored his first Test century just three weeks shy of his 28th birthday in August 2018.

players.name: Harry Brook
players.bio:
A former Under-19 England captain, Harry Brook made his Test debut in 2022 after averaging over 100 for Yorkshire in the County Championship.

He thrashed Pakistan in his first Test tour, belting 153 in his second Test, 108 in his third and 111 in his fourth.

A member of England’s T20 World Cup-winning side in 2022, Brook became a staple in all formats for the national side.

His impact was negated somewhat during the 2023 Ashes campaign, managing four half-centuries in five Tests as England drew the series 2-2.

In October 2024, Brook returned to Pakistan and joined an elite club by scoring 317 from 322 deliveries - the second-fastest triple century behind only Virender Sehwag.

In 2025, Brook was installed as England’s white-ball captain, replacing Jos Buttler, after the team’s early exit from that year’s Champions Trophy.

players.name: Jacob Bethell
players.bio:
Born in Bridgetown, Barbados, Bethell moved to England aged 12 on a private school scholarship, and was soon signed up by Edgbaston-based county Warwickshire, making his List A and County Championship debuts in 2021.

He made his T20 International debut against Australia in September 2024, hitting Adam Zampa for a 20-run over to help England to a win in Cardiff, and played all five matches in the following ODI series. His maiden ODI century against South Africa was his first ton in any List A cricket.

A Test debut on tour of New Zealand followed as he earned caps in three formats in the space of four months, scoring fifties in each of his first three Test appearances.

Drafted by the Melbourne Renegades with pick 10 of the BBL|14 draft before he had made his international debut, he played eight games with a high score of 87 in the 2024-25 summer.

He was named England's youngest ever international captain for a T20 series against Ireland in Dublin, aged 21 years and 329 days.

He was parachuted back into England's Test XI at No.3 in place of Ollie Pope after the Ashes were lost on the 2025-26 tour of Australia, playing the final two matches of the series. He hit his maiden Test century in second innings of the fifth Test in Sydney, which was also his maiden hundred in any first-class cricket, making him the first specialist England batter to achieve that feat, and the first from England to do it in the Test and ODI formats.

players.name: Tom Banton
players.bio:
Tom Banton is one of the rising stars of English cricket and has been secured by the Brisbane Heat until the end of BBL|11. In his inaugural Big Bash season, he smashed three half centuries at a team high strike rate of 176.98 in his haul of 223 runs.

He thrashed the second fastest half century of all time in the BBL during the rain-affected clash with the Sydney Thunder, scoring 50 from just 16 balls including hitting five sixes in an over.

players.name: Will Jacks
players.bio:
A tall allrounder who can hit a long ball, Will Jacks has become a hot commodity on the T20 circuit with his desirable attributes.

Now an all-format England representative, Jacks played a season with Hobart Hurricanes in BBL|10 but failed to impress with 79 runs in eight innings.

Since then however, things have clicked for Jacks and he has hit a century in the Indian Premier League, the Hundred, T20 Blast, SA20 and Bangladesh Premier League.

He made his Test debut in Rawalpindi, taking 6-161 on debut against Pakistan playing as a bowling allrounder under the new leadership of Brendon McCullum. However, he lost his spot after going wicketless in his next three innings.

He was a surprise inclusion for England's Ashes squad to Australia in 2025-26, named as Shoaib Bashir's spin back up option.

players.name: Liam Dawson
players.bio:
Liam Dawson has had little international experience in England’s top team, however has had numerous appearances for the England Lions.

Holding impressive numbers with bat and ball at first-class level, Dawson had yet to make his senior international debut for England when selected in the squad for the 2016 World T20 in India.

Since then, Dawson has debuted in every format for England, making an unbeaten 66 in Test cricket, his highest international score to date.

players.name: Jofra Archer
players.bio:
Born in Bridgetown, Barbados, Jofra Archer is a fast bowler capable of reaching eye-watering speeds and on his day among the best in the world.

He represented West Indies Under-19s in 2013 but thanks to his British passport due to his English father, Archer soon made it clear he wanted to represent England, not West Indies.

Before his international breakthrough, Archer had two highly successful years with Hobart Hurricanes in the BBL, where he instantly became a fan favourite and a match-winner.

After some controversy surrounding his qualification for England's national side, Archer was rushed into the World Cup squad in 2019 where he became an integral member of the XI, culminating in bowling the Super Over in the tied final against New Zealand.

His introduction to the Test arena was equally thrilling, concussing Australia's Steve Smith with a short ball during the 2019 Lord's Test before going on to take 22 wickets in the pulsating drawn Ashes series.

Injuries saw Archer miss two years of international cricket between 2021 and 2023 before he was eased back into the national white-ball sides. In July 2025, Archer ended a four-year spell in the Test wilderness when he returned for the Lord's Test against India.

players.name: Adil Rashid
players.bio:
Adil Rashid is an important member of the England limited-overs teams, with the leg-spinning Yorkshireman showing good sings in ODIs and T20Is. 

Born in England with a Pakistani background, Rashid made his T20I debut in 2009 against the Netherlands. However it was in 2015 where the right-arm spinner made his Test debut, taking a five-wicket haul against the very nation his family were from. 

Australian cricket fans will remember Rashid’s superb bowling for Adelaide Strikers in BBL|05, finishing the regular season in second spot on the Official Bowler Rankings under the guidance of Yorkshire coach Jason Gillespie.

players.name: Hardik Pandya
players.bio:
Hardik Pandya made his international debut for India against Australia in 2016.

His ODI debut came later that year against New Zealand, while he made his Test debut in 2017 against Sri Lanka where he made a half-century in his first innings.

players.name: Axar Patel
players.didyouKnow: He wanted to be an engineer before his father encouraged him to play competitive cricket.
players.bio:
Not many people had heard of Akshar Patel before the 2014 Indian Premier League when the allrounder impressed for Kings XI Punjab with 17 wickets and was named emerging player of the tournament.

That performance brought the off-spinner to the attention of national selectors and Patel made his one-day international debut against Bangladesh in June 2014.

Patel, made his competitive debut in early 2012 playing for his home state Gujarat and was one of the key players in India under-23's title win in the ACC Emerging Teams Cup 2013.

Patel played a crucial hand in the 2024 T20 World Cup final against South Africa, hitting four sixes in his quickfire innings of 47 off 31, helping India win their first senior ICC tournament in over a decade.

players.name: Arshdeep Singh
players.bio:
Arshdeep Singh made his international debut in a T20I against England in 2022.

The left-arm quick has been used as a white-ball specialist by India, with his speed and ability to consistently hit the yorker length deployed to good effect in the death overs regularly.

Arshdeep made a mark on the international stage instantly, achieving the rare feat of starting with a maiden over in his first-ever match.

He has since gone on to become first and the fastest Indian bowler to take 100 wickets in Men's T20Is.

A highlight of Arshdeep's career came at the MCG in 2022. Playing his first T20 World Cup game, a high-pressure encounter against arch-rivals Pakistan, the young fast bowler removed opposition captain Babar Azam on a golden duck with his very first ball. He followed it up with the wicket of the other opener, Mohammad Rizwan, in his next over.

The Punjab player finished as the leading wicket-taker for his team in that tournament. In the next edition of the T20 World Cup in 2024, he was the overall join-highest wicket taker for the tournament, taking 17 scalps. He was also named in the ICC Team of the Tournament.

Arshdeep is currently India's highest wicket-taker in Men’s T20Is, having overtaken Yuzvendra Chahal in 2025.

players.name: Jasprit Bumrah
players.didyouKnow: On Boxing Day 2018, Bumrah became the first Asian bowler to take five wickets in Australia, England and South Africa in the same calendar year.
players.bio:
Jasprit Bumrah is on all levels a unique bowler. With a lackadaisical approach to the wicket, sometimes off no more than six paces, Bumrah is renowned as one of the most lethal fast bowlers across formats.

Bumrah emerged in Australia in 2016 as a limited-overs talent making both his ODI and T20I debuts against Australia within the space of four days.

He was an immediate success, and after years of great results with Mumbai Indians in the IPL, the longest format beckoned for Bumrah.

After Steve Smith (ODI) and David Warner (T20) were his first wickets in white-ball internationals, he claimed the scalp of AB de Villiers for his first Test wicket in January 2018 and took another 47 more wickets in the year to come.

He followed that up with a memorable 2018-19 summer against Australia, taking career-best figures of 6-33 in the Boxing Day Test as India won the Border-Gavaskar Trophy on Aussie soil.


He became the first bowler from an Asian nation to take five-wicket hauls in Australia, England and South Africa in the same year.


In 2022 Bumrah captained India in the fifth Test against England, finishing that campaign as player of the series with 23 wickets.

The unorthodox bowler was massive during India’s 2023 ODI World Cup run and 2024 T20 World Cup success, named player of the series in the latter for his 15 wickets at 8.26 and 2-18 in the final.
